questions.q: What is the single most important metric for a Cosmos DB workload, per this lesson?
options: The number of containers in the account
Total Storage — how much disk space is used
Total Request Units — the rough equivalent of watching CPU/IO on a SQL Server instance
Network latency between regions only
questions.explain: RU consumption is the core currency of Cosmos DB cost and throughput, making Total Request Units the headline metric.

questions.q: What does Normalized RU Consumption tell you?
options: The number of regions the account is distributed across
The total dollar cost of the Cosmos DB account
The exact number of documents stored in a container
The percentage of provisioned throughput actually being used — the fastest signal for whether a container is under- or over-provisioned
questions.explain: A container running near 100% is under-provisioned (hot); a consistently low percentage suggests over-provisioning.

questions.q: What is the practical difference between metrics and diagnostic logs in Cosmos DB monitoring?
options: Metrics tell you that something happened (aggregated trends); diagnostic logs tell you what actually happened, request by request
Metrics and diagnostic logs are identical, just different names for the same data
Diagnostic logs only cover storage, never request activity
Metrics require Log Analytics, but diagnostic logs don't
questions.explain: Metrics are aggregated trend data; diagnostic logs capture per-request detail like RU charge, status code, and duration for individual operations.

questions.q: What query language is used to analyze Cosmos DB diagnostic logs once routed to Log Analytics?
options: T-SQL
Cypher
KQL (Kusto Query Language)
The Cosmos DB SQL query language itself
questions.explain: Log Analytics uses KQL, letting a DBA query actual request history instead of guessing what's expensive.

questions.q: What does this lesson identify as a reasonable production monitoring baseline for Cosmos DB?
options: Monitoring is unnecessary for a managed PaaS service like Cosmos DB
Only check the Storage metric, since RU-related metrics aren't actionable
Route diagnostic logs to Log Analytics, set alerts on normalized RU consumption and 429 rate, and build a dashboard surfacing RU trends per container
Rely exclusively on third-party monitoring tools, since Azure-native tooling is insufficient
questions.explain: This baseline uses only built-in Azure-native tooling — no third-party tools required.
